newsitem.title: GERMANY: Petrolub makes offer for Swiss unit.
newsitem.headline: Petrolub makes offer for Swiss unit.

text.p: Germany's Fuchs Petrolub Oel + Chemie AG said on Wednesday it was making an offer to swap its shares for the publicly-held minority in its Swiss unit Fuch Petrolub AG.

The Mannheim-based lubricating oil company, which owns 53.7 percent of the Swiss subsidiary, said in a regulatory news release the share swap would optimise the group's structure and significantly increase shareholder value.
Details of the exchange offer will be made in March, and it would apply to all 360,000 shares in public float and would be worth 500 Swiss francs per share.
That is 21.6 percent above the weighted average price of the past 12 months, and 15.2 percent higher than the Zurich closing price on January 28, the statement continued.
The offer will probably be made up of shares in the German parent, plus a cash payment.
An extraordinary general meeting is planned to be held in Mannheim on April 23. If approval is granted by shareholders in the German parent company, the offer will be made.
